clues.text: During the feast in Jerusalem, the Roman governor was holding him as a notorious prisoner.
He had been thrown into prison in Jerusalem for an uprising in the city and for murder.
While Pilate governed Judea, this man sat in prison alongside rebels who had committed murder in a revolt.
The chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds before Pilate to ask for this prisoner's release.
Shouting at Pilate about Jesus, the crowd cried as one, "Away with this man!" and demanded him freed instead.
Pilate set him free, then had Jesus flogged and handed over to be crucified.
He walked free in Jerusalem under the Jewish custom of having one prisoner released at Passover.
